review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the proofs with each other. I also grepped the repo for openPCoreOf_subgroupOf, which is already a one-line API lemma. Several blocks look repeated but are too short to justify a helper under this rubric: the `hOsub` setup, the `Fact (Nat.Prime 2)`/E/π preamble, the symmetric A/B branches in `indecomposable`, and the `le_normalizer_pCoreOf` side goals. The only repeated reasoning with real content is the transport of a commutator condition from `pCoreOf 2 H` in Q to `CFSG.pCore 2 ↥H` in the subgroup. It occurs in `mem_pCoreOf_of_pow_two_mem` and `isNilpotent_bar2_of_upperTwo_central`. I have not compiled the proposed lemma, and the gain is modest, so this finding is low-confidence.

findings.problem: Two proofs repeat the same transfer step. A commutator ⁅x,y⁆ of elements of ↥H, whose image in Q lies in O, is moved into E = CFSG.pCore 2 ↥H. Each proof does it by pushing `H.subtype` through the commutator with `map_commutatorElement`, then casting through `Subgroup.mem_subgroupOf` along `hOsub`. In `mem_pCoreOf_of_pow_two_mem` the result feeds `(QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr (hmemE g)` to show π tH is central. In `isNilpotent_bar2_of_upperTwo_central` it feeds `(QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr hmemE` to show the image of ⁅J,⊤⁆ is trivial. Both proofs also repeat the `hOsub : O.subgroupOf H = E` setup and the `set E`/`let π` preamble. The maintenance cost is that the Q-to-↥H-to-Bar2 bookkeeping is spelled out twice inside long proofs.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma before `mem_pCoreOf_of_pow_two_mem`:
`private theorem map_commutator_eq_one_of_mem {H O : Subgroup Q} (hOsub : O.subgroupOf H = CFSG.pCore 2 ↥H) (x y : ↥H) (h : ⁅(x : Q), (y : Q)⁆ ∈ O) : (QuotientGroup.mk' (CFSG.pCore 2 ↥H)) ⁅x, y⁆ = 1`.
Proof sketch: `h` rewrites to `H.subtype ⁅x,y⁆ ∈ O` by `map_commutatorElement`. Then `Subgroup.mem_subgroupOf` and `hOsub` give `⁅x,y⁆ ∈ pCore 2 ↥H`. Finish with `(QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr`.
Use in `mem_pCoreOf_of_pow_two_mem`: `hcomm` becomes `rw [← map_commutatorElement]; exact map_commutator_eq_one_of_mem hOsub tH g (hc _ g.2)`. Here `hOsub` is the existing one with O = pCoreOf 2 P, and `hc` supplies the membership.
Use in `isNilpotent_bar2_of_upperTwo_central`: the `hker` body becomes `exact map_commutator_eq_one_of_mem hOsub x y (Subgroup.commutator_le.mp hJL _ hxJ _ y.2)`.
The same lemma could also replace the open-coded steps in the other file-local uses of `hOsub`, if any.
findings.benefit: The Q-level to subgroup-level to quotient transfer is stated and proved once. Both callers shrink to the actual mathematical input: commutators of L i with t, or of J with H, lie in the 2-core. A future change to the `Bar2` or `pCore` API then needs one edit instead of two. The gain is modest because each block is short, so this is a low-priority cleanup.
